clips.text: A stranger stubs his toe across the street — and the pain shoots through YOUR foot.
For one person in sixty, that is not empathy. That is an ordinary Tuesday. Every handshake, every slap, every hug echoes on their skin.
Your brain already simulates other people's pain. In the lab, sixteen couples proved it: the emotional half of the pain network lights up when a loved one is hurt.
In one person in sixty, the simulation crosses the line. A doctor feels his patients' spinal taps in his own back.
Horror movies become unbearable. A stranger's grief sits in your chest. There is no off switch.
A stranger stubs his toe across the street — and the pain shoots through YOUR foot. Would you keep the gift, or give it back?
